description: The most recent reported value of each metric for one ticker, each with its period (fy, fp), period end, filing date and form. Each metric is its own latest value, so two metrics can come from different periods, and a quarterly fp means ONE quarter's figure, not a year. Pass as_of to use only filings dated on or before that day (how each market dates a filing: https://www.tradingagentapp.com/fundamentals/methodology). On a free key, a company outside the full-history sample answers from its most recent reported fiscal year only (history_depth says so) and as_of needs a licence or an evaluation key. Tickers look like AAPL, 2330.TW, 005930.KS, 0403091220.BE, 775670417.FR, CC21860.NZC (and 10238429.EE, 5560021361.SE, 47239255.SK, 40003032949.LV where the coverage lists them). Suffixes are not all listed equities, and not all figures mean what the column name suggests. .TW income-statement values are SINGLE-QUARTER (three-month) amounts: Taiwan files cumulative year-to-date totals and they are converted before you see them, so do NOT difference adjacent quarters again. A .TW row with fp FY is the full-year total, not a quarter. .TW current quarters come from the TWSE OpenAPI (Open Government Data License v1.0, attribution required); history from 2013 comes from the TWSE MOPS XBRL archive, which is NOT open data: keep both attribution notices and do not call Taiwan figures open data. US figures (SEC EDGAR) are public information. .TW filing dates are the statutory reporting deadline, a proxy, not the actual release date; for some financial and foreign first-listed companies and for weekend deadlines it can be earlier than the real deadline (known issue, being corrected). .BE is Belgian STATUTORY SOLO accounts, never group consolidation. .NZC is New Zealand REGISTERED CHARITIES (Charities Register annual returns), not listed companies; their `filed` is the register's record date, and about a quarter of those are one day early (known issue, being corrected). .FR is INPI's register of keyed-in annual accounts: `filed` is dateDepot, the register's own deposit date, and balance sheets are included. Coverage is substantially complete from 2022; 2017-2021 is still backfilling. Turnover is lawfully absent from roughly 36% of French deposits (confidentiality declarations); it is PRESENT on 64.0% of company-periods, and the API's /api/v1/fundamentals/quality endpoint reports the measured share of every metric in every market. The reporting model rides in `form` (K consolidated, C complet, S simplifie); consolidated and own accounts are separate deposits with their own dates, so both can appear for one SIREN and period. .DK `filed` is the Copenhagen calendar date of the register's publication, a date only before 11 April 2015; Danish history starts in June 2012. .DK figures are the reporting entity's own accounts: for a Danish-GAAP parent that also publishes group accounts, usually its own figures, not the group's; for an IFRS filer (form annual/ifrs), the consolidated group's. .DK turnover is present on only 10.6% of company-periods (Belgium is lower still at 8.1%) because Danish reporting class B may publish gross profit instead — that absence is lawful disclosure, not missing data, and gross profit is never a substitute for it. A .DK `form` is annual (Danish GAAP) or annual/ifrs, with the period's length appended when a year is not 11-13 months (annual/15m for a long first year); /liquidation marks accounts drawn up in liquidation and /correction a period the register holds only as a corrected report; /same-as-adjacent, always last, marks both of two adjacent annual periods whose figures are identical (the filer may have repeated another year's figures; they are served as filed, and the flag does not say which period, if either, is wrong); interim reports are excluded. .EE is the Estonian e-Business Register (companies, associations and foundations that file an annual report; CC BY 4.0): `filed` is the date the register records the report as submitted, an Estonian calendar date; figures are the company's own (basis solo) and, where the register's key-figure file has them, a consolidated report's group figures ride beside them with basis consolidated (form …/consolidated); about 1,900 reports, many of them consolidated and among them those of banks and listed groups, are not included, because the register, not the filer, enters their key figures manually after the report is submitted, so the submission date does not date those figures, and some companies have no figures here at all (known issue); form annual/pdf marks a turnover, assets or employee-count figure taken only from the separate boxes the filer keys in (the register's PDF key figures), not from the report's statements; a report filed only as a PDF carries just those figures; employees is in full-time equivalents (unit FTE). .SE is Bolagsverket's digitally submitted annual reports from 2020: `filed` is the Sunday ending the week (Monday to Sunday) in which the bulk file places the report, a proxy for its registration date: expected not to be earlier than registration and up to six days later, not yet compared report by report with the registration date (known issue); liabilities exclude untaxed reserves (untaxed_reserves). For .EE and .SE the response's `attributes` gives the industry code with its source and date, and for .EE the shareholders that are legal persons; natural persons and sole proprietors are never included, so that list is never the full ownership. With as_of, an attribute known only as of a later date is left out and named in attributes.withheld_after_as_of. .SK is the Slovak Register účtovných závierok (RÚZ, CC0): structured statements of companies and other legal persons from financial year 2019; `filed` is the later of the statement's filing date and the last day the register changed the report holding the figures, so never before the filing date and usually a day or so after it; micro entities (form annual/micro) report revenue as sales of goods plus own products and services; IFRS statements filed only as PDF, among them many of the largest companies, are not included, nor are banks', insurers', funds' and public bodies' statements or single-entry statements. .LV is the Latvian Register of Enterprises' annual-report data (CC0), financial periods ending 2020 or later: the files state no filing date, so `filed` is the Riga calendar date the register's data record of the report was created, a proxy read as UTC (the register's own files indicate Riga local time, so it can be one day later than the record's creation, never earlier), which can be later than the filing, by an amount the files do not show, and as far as we know never earlier; the files do not show changes, so a report changed before we first collected it is held in its changed version; associations and foundations are not included. Natural persons who are entrepreneurs are never included for either. Period labels: fp is FY for an annual row; for a quarterly row (US, Taiwan) fy and fp are the CALENDAR year and quarter that contain the period end, not the company's own fiscal quarter: Apple's quarter ending 2025-12-27 is 2025 Q4, which Apple calls Q1 of fiscal 2026, so name a quarter by its period end, not by the label. A latest-view fact with a quarterly fp is ONE quarter's figure, not a full year. Licence: when you relay figures, keep the `attribution` notices and the `licence` notice of the response with them.

as_of.description: Filing-date cut-off, YYYY-MM-DD (e.g. 2022-01-01). Defaults to today.
